name: Myofunctional therapy
lead: Orofacial myofunctional therapy (OMT) is a program of exercises for the tongue, lips, cheeks and throat muscles, used clinically for conditions such as obstructive sleep apnea, tongue dysfunction and open bite, and discussed in looksmaxxing communities in connection with tongue posture and jaw development.[1][4]

A systematic review and meta-analysis of myofunctional therapy for obstructive sleep apnea examined polysomnographic, snoring and sleepiness outcomes in children and adults.[1] Further studies examine its use alongside CPAP, in children with sleep-disordered breathing, and in orthodontic cases.[3][5][6][7] Evidence concerns airway and function; no trial located for this entry has tested it for facial appearance.
infobox: Sleep apnea, tongue dysfunction, open bite

paras: Therapy programs promote changes in the musculature of the upper airway and mouth, and published reviews summarize the programs used and their possible mechanisms.[4]

A 2015 systematic review and meta-analysis pooled studies in children and adults.[1] An ERS guideline on non-CPAP therapies for sleep apnea includes it among the options reviewed.[2] A 2017 study examined whether myofunctional therapy improves adherence to CPAP.[3]

Studies have examined myofunctional reeducation in children with sleep-disordered breathing,[5][6] a pilot study in children with anterior open bite and tongue dysfunction,[7] and relapse of open bites treated with appliances with and without therapy.[8]

On looksmax.org, users have asked whether jaw-growth devices and myofunctional exercises are pseudoscience, after a consultation that likened them to mewing.[9] Mewing is described by reference sources as unproven, with the American Association of Orthodontists stating there is no evidence it improves the jaw.[10]
Studies cited above cover sleep apnea, CPAP adherence, pediatric sleep-disordered breathing and open bite.[1][3][5][6][7][8] None located for this entry assessed facial appearance as an outcome.

lore.intro: Forum discussion links myofunctional therapy to tongue posture and jaw exercises.[9]

claims.claim: Myofunctional exercises can move a recessed jaw forward
claims.believers: A user reports a consultation in which clinicians described gaining several millimetres of forward movement through exercises and a device, linking it to posture.[9]
claims.experts: Published studies address airway and function outcomes; no study located tested jaw position change for appearance.[1][4]

card.summary: Tongue and mouth exercises with sleep-apnea evidence; no evidence it changes facial looks.
card.note: Evidence is for airway outcomes, not appearance.

quick.overview:
Myofunctional therapy is a set of tongue, lip and throat exercises used clinically for sleep apnea, tongue dysfunction and open bite. Looksmaxxers discuss it alongside tongue posture and mewing.

Systematic reviews exist for sleep apnea; none located tests it for facial appearance.
quick.mechanism: Exercises aim to change tone and function of the upper airway and oral muscles.
quick.risks: No notable risks are described in the sources consulted. Sleep apnea is a medical condition managed by clinicians.
